newsitem.title: ITALY: Cariplo says why it chose Ambroveneto.
newsitem.headline: Cariplo says why it chose Ambroveneto.

text.p: The chairman of the charitable foundation that owns Italian savings bank Cariplo said it agreed to merge with Banco Ambrosiano Veneto because of its stable share ownership and good branch network.

Giuseppe Guzzetti told Italian business weekly Mondo Economico in an interview released ahead of publication that it had rejected a rival bid from BCI because it was concentrated in areas which were of less interest to Cariplo.

Cariplo was also attracted by Ambroveneto's international connections through its main shareholder Credit Agricole -- "the first banking group in Europe which through Indosuez has a presence in 60 countries," Guzzetti was quoted as saying.
He said it also was not clear to Cariplo who exactly controlled BCI.

"Comit (BCI) told us that some of its important shareholders wanted to merge the two banks. But what are the arrangements for controlling Comit? And what guarantees of stability are there?" he said, adding "for a foundation these are elements which carry weight."
He said BCI's international operation was not particularly appealing. "Comit (BCI) is the Italian bank with the biggest presence abroad, with 336 branches but 300 are in South America," he added.
"Comit does not have such strong roots in the areas that interest us," Guzzetti said.

Turning to the Cariplo foundation's own future, Guzzetti said it would have to identify sectors in which to invest the 6.5 trillion lire it would raise from the alliance with Ambroveneto, which was announced on Monday.
"I would not want the foundations to be thrust into state companies which are due for privatisation once they (the foundations) have withdrawn from the banks," he said.
